sex.evidence: Male Swiss-Webster mice (CFW; Charles River Laboratories, Inc.; Wilmington, MA) served as the subjects of all in vivo experiments.

dosing.evidence: (+/-)-2,5-Dimethoxy-4-iodoamphetamine (DOI) was synthesized at the Research Triangle Institute (Research Triangle Park, NC) and dissolved in normal saline. ... Vehicle or DOI (3 mg/kg) was administered ... acute treatment ... also administered immediately following removal ... for each of the four afternoon ethanol conditioning sessions ... subchronic treatment.

group_housing.evidence: With the exception of the two-bottle choice study, all mice were housed in groups of 4

day_night_flipped.evidence: The lights were turned off at 7 p.m. every evening and turned back on at 7 a.m. every morning, and experiments were conducted during the light phase

assays.assay_description: Video recorded head-twitches from 5 to 15 min after DOI (1, 3, or 10 mg/kg, i.p.) injection; raw count of twitches per animal.

application_type.evidence: DOI was dissolved in normal saline and administered intraperitoneally

setup_restrain.evidence: HTR behavior was video recorded in each subject; standard HTR is unrestrained

food_restriction.evidence: Standard HTR chamber; food not present in recording apparatus

water_restriction.evidence: Standard HTR chamber; water not present in recording apparatus

time_to_assay.evidence: HTR behavior was video recorded in each subject from 5 to 15 min after the injection of (+/-)-DOI

outcomes.summary: DOI produced an inverted-U dose-response for head twitches, with 3 mg/kg inducing significantly more head twitches than either 1 or 10 mg/kg.
outcomes.evidence: we found a main effect of (+/-)-DOI on the HTR (F 2,23 = 19.79; p < 0.001), with a dose of 3 mg/kg inducing significantly more head twitches than either 1 (q = 8.614) or 10 (q = 6.238) mg/kg (p < 0.001)

B1_num_measures.evidence: The head-twitch response is expressed as a raw count

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Counts were summed over the 5-15 min window

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is explicitly excluded from ethological behaviours per rubric

B5_social.evidence: Individual testing, not a social assay

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Head-twitches counted from video, no ML classifier reported

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water present during HTR recording

D2_session_duration.evidence: from 5 to 15 min after the injection (10 min window)

assays.assay_description: Ethanol-induced (1.8 g/kg) CPP in plastic 46x30 cm two-compartment boxes. 2 days habituation (30 min/day), 15-min pretest, 4 days conditioning (2 sessions/day), 15-min post-test. DOI (3 mg/kg) given acutely 30 min before post-test or subchronically immediately after each conditioning session.

application_type.evidence: Vehicle or DOI (3 mg/kg) was administered 30 min prior to introduction of the mouse to the CPP chamber

setup_habituation.evidence: Prior to conditioning, mice underwent 2 days of habituation with a 30-min session each day, where they had unrestricted access to both sides of the chamber

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were placed freely in the CPP apparatus

food_restriction.evidence: Standard CPP apparatus, no food present during test

water_restriction.evidence: Standard CPP apparatus, no water present during test

time_to_assay.evidence: Vehicle or DOI (3 mg/kg) was administered 30 min prior to introduction of the mouse to the CPP chamber during the final post-test session

outcomes.summary: Ethanol (1.8 g/kg) induced a significant CPP in saline-treated mice. Both acute (30 min pre-test) and subchronic (post-conditioning) treatment with DOI (3 mg/kg) prevented the expression of ethanol CPP.
outcomes.evidence: both acute or subchronic treatment with DOI prevented the expression of ethanol CPP

B1_num_measures.evidence: The proportion of time spent in the less preferred compartment served as the dependent measure of conditioning

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Only total proportion of session time reported

B4_ethological.evidence: Time in zone is a spatial measure, not ethological

B6_cognitive.evidence: CPP requires learning of a drug-context association

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Med Associates soundproof boxes; no ML behavioural classifier reported

E1_environment_type.evidence: CPP experiments were performed in plastic 46 cm × 30 cm boxes

E2_shelter.evidence: Two open compartments of equal size, no shelter

E3_bedding.evidence: Different floor textures (smooth versus hole board); no bedding

E6_spatial.evidence: each separated by a removable partition into two compartments of equal size

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in CPP apparatus

D1_continuity.evidence: 15-min pretest and 15-min post-test on different days

D2_session_duration.evidence: 2 days of habituation with a 30-min session each day

D3_recording_days.evidence: Habituation (2 days), pretest (day 3), 4 days conditioning, post-test

D4_baseline.evidence: On the third day, mice were placed in the chamber for a 15-min pretest with unrestricted access to establish which environment was preferred

D5_followup.evidence: Post-test occurred shortly after final conditioning

assays.assay_description: Individually housed mice given intermittent access (M/W/F) to 20% v/v ethanol and water. DOI (3 mg/kg, i.p.) or saline administered 30 min before ethanol provision; M100907 (0.1 mg/kg) given 15 min before DOI. Ethanol intake, preference, and total fluid intake assessed at 1 h and 24 h. Mice split into high vs low drinkers.

application_type.evidence: mice were injected with DOI (3 mg/kg) or saline intraperitoneally 30 min prior to the provision of ethanol

setup_habituation.evidence: Acquisition phase but apparatus habituation not explicitly described

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice drank freely in home cage

food_restriction.evidence: Animals had access to food (Laboratory Rodent Diet) and water ad libitum

water_restriction.evidence: one containing water and the other containing ethanol... animal allowed to drink overnight

time_to_assay.evidence: mice were injected with DOI (3 mg/kg) or saline intraperitoneally 30 min prior to the provision of ethanol

sample_size.evidence: high drinking group (N = 10) and a low drinking group (N = 9)

outcomes.summary: DOI (3 mg/kg) significantly suppressed ethanol intake at 24 h and decreased ethanol preference at 1 h and 24 h in high-drinking mice; effects reversed by 5-HT2A antagonist M100907. No effect on total fluid intake. No effect of DOI on intake, preference, or fluid intake in low-drinking mice.
outcomes.evidence: DOI significantly suppressed ethanol intake relative to the saline injection (q = 5.946, p < 0.01), which was reversed (p < 0.05) by pretreatment with the selective 5-HT2A receptor antagonist M100907

B1_num_measures.evidence: Ethanol intake, preference for ethanol, and total fluid intake

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Two between-session timepoints (1h, 24h), not within-session dynamics

B4_ethological.evidence: Drinking volume is not listed among the ethological behaviours per rubric

B6_cognitive.evidence: Voluntary consumption model, no learning component

E1_environment_type.evidence: mice weighed between 25 and 55 g and were housed individually to collect individual drinking data

E3_bedding.evidence: Standard home-cage bedding present during home-cage testing

E7_social_context.evidence: Mice housed individually to collect individual drinking data

E8_food_water.evidence: presented with two 25-ml pipette bottles fitted with stainless steel metal sippers, with one containing water and the other containing ethanol

D1_continuity.evidence: Acquisition (~9 sessions) + treatment sessions on Mondays with assessments at 1h and 24h

D2_session_duration.evidence: animal allowed to drink overnight; measured at 1 h and 24 h

D3_recording_days.evidence: Stable drinking typically emerged within 9 sessions, after which mice were divided into the high and low drinking groups

D4_baseline.evidence: Baseline drinking established during acquisition before DOI administration

D5_followup.evidence: Ethanol consumption and preference were assessed 1 h and 24 h after the provision of ethanol

D6_circadian.evidence: animal allowed to drink overnight; 24-h measurement window

assays.assay_description: Mice given DOI (3 mg/kg) or saline 15 min before ethanol (3 g/kg, i.p.). 10 min after ethanol, placed supine in a plastic trough; time to recover three righting responses within 30 s was measured.

application_type.evidence: Mice (N = 8 per group) were administered saline or DOI (3 mg/kg) 15 min prior to the injection of ethanol

setup_restrain.evidence: each mouse was placed in the supine position in a plastic trough; recovery measured by righting, not restraint

food_restriction.evidence: No food in plastic trough during LORR measurement

water_restriction.evidence: No water in plastic trough during LORR measurement

time_to_assay.evidence: administered saline or DOI (3 mg/kg) 15 min prior to the injection of ethanol

outcomes.summary: DOI (3 mg/kg) significantly increased the duration of loss of righting reflex induced by 3 g/kg ethanol, indicating enhanced ethanol sedation.
outcomes.evidence: DOI significantly (T 6 = 4.08; p < 0.01) increased sensitivity to the sedating effects of ethanol as assessed by paired t test

B1_num_measures.evidence: Recovery time from LORR was the only dependent measure

B4_ethological.evidence: Righting reflex is not an ethological behaviour

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in trough

D2_session_duration.evidence: Recovery from a 3 g/kg ethanol dose typically extends beyond 15 min; specific duration not stated

judge_notes: Dropped non-behavioural outputs: blood ethanol pharmacokinetics (physiological sampling) and the RAW264.7 macrophage nitric oxide assay (in vitro cell culture) — neither is a rodent behavioural assay.
Retained four assays: HTR, CPP (acute + subchronic DOI collapsed into one CPP entry per rubric), two-bottle choice (high + low drinkers and M100907 antagonist collapsed into one entry), and LORR.

DOI schedule classified as 'repeated' because the CPP subchronic arm administered DOI on 4 consecutive conditioning days; HTR/2BC/LORR involved acute doses but the study-level schedule entry covers all administrations.

Two-bottle choice E3 bedding scored Yes (home-cage testing with standard bedding present), D6 circadian scored Yes (overnight drinking spans >6 h), D2 scored 2 (61 min–6 h boundary; the 24-h measurement window is the longest continuous bout but rubric caps practical home-cage drinking sessions here).
Age scored not_reported: only body weights (25–40 g) were given, no age in days or weeks.
DOI sex_dependent and time_dependent set to n/a where only one sex/timepoint relevant; CPP time_dependent = no because acute and subchronic both blocked CPP.
